name: Rantepao
tagline: The lively hub town at the heart of Toraja tourism
description: Rantepao is the main base for visitors, with the region's best cluster of guesthouses, warung, cafes with wifi, and the central market that draws traders from surrounding villages. It's compact and walkable, with drivers and guides easy to arrange right from your accommodation. Most excursions to villages and burial sites start here.
bestFor: first-time visitors, arranging tours and drivers
pros: Best concentration of guesthouses and eateries
Easiest place to arrange drivers, guides, and motorbikes
cons: Traffic and noise around the market and main roads
Still limited, unreliable wifi despite being the most connected town

name: Makale
tagline: The quieter administrative capital, 20 minutes south of Rantepao
description: Makale is South Toraja's regency capital, calmer and less tourist-oriented than Rantepao, with a central town square, government offices, and a more local, workaday feel. It makes a decent low-key alternative base with a handful of decent hotels, and is closer to some southern burial sites and villages than Rantepao is.
bestFor: travelers wanting a calmer, less touristy base
pros: Fewer tourists, more authentic daily-life feel
Closer to some southern cultural sites
Generally quieter for rest and work
cons: Fewer tourist-oriented cafes and services than Rantepao

name: Kete Kesu
tagline: A living traditional village with tongkonan houses and ancient hanging graves
description: Just south of Rantepao, Kete Kesu is one of the best-preserved traditional Torajan villages, with a row of centuries-old tongkonan houses, rice barns, and a cliffside burial site featuring hanging coffins and bamboo bone piles. It remains inhabited, offering a genuine look at how tongkonan architecture is still used today.
bestFor: photography, learning about tongkonan architecture and burial customs
cons: Can feel touristy with vendor stalls near the entrance

name: Lemo and Londa burial sites
tagline: Dramatic cliffside grave galleries watched over by tau-tau effigies
description: South of Rantepao, Lemo and Londa are the region's most striking burial sites: sheer rock faces carved with balconies of tau-tau wooden effigies overlooking the valley, plus cave burial chambers at Londa accessible with a local guide and lantern. These sites anchor most half-day cultural tours out of Rantepao.
bestFor: understanding Torajan burial traditions and tau-tau effigies
pros: Visually striking, unlike anywhere else in Indonesia
Guides on-site explain customs and history well
Combinable in a single half-day tour
cons: Requires a hired driver or tour, no public transport
Sites can feel solemn; visitors should be respectful, not just snap photos
